placements.why: Reinforces the core installable expertise paradigm: extracting citable perspective as a technical moat, targeting non-tech knowledge businesses rather than self-building developers, containing context fragmentation across concurrent AI workspaces, isolating the human lens as the controlling core, and evaluating intermediary network moats against incumbent replication.

Expands pricing and packaging strategy by positioning lower tiers for solo builders acting as single-person teams, while defining the enterprise plan by deployment architecture and organizational needs rather than enterprise client labeling.

Applies the interview flywheel thesis by proposing a podcast format that simultaneously conducts expert interviews, creates public content, and packages installable expertise to populate the marketplace.
Reasserts the foundational principle that authentic human emotional moments and live reactions drive sales and demonstrate value far more effectively than static textual artifacts.
Frames early fundraising strategy and operational focus around strategic environment awareness, urging the founder to shift from continuous product development to active market selling.
